trust_decision.summary: On Watch create the server decides whether the caller may observe the range [Key, RangeEnd) by calling authStore.IsRangePermitted (server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/watch.go:296 via :246), which classifies len(rangeEnd)==0 as an exact-key point query (server/auth/range_perm_cache.go:124) and otherwise requires the user's permission interval to contain the requested interval (:73-95); at the pinned commit the handler rewrote the open-ended 0x00 sentinel into []byte{} (:270-278) before that call, so an open-ended '>= key' watch was authorized as a point read.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the Watch API and the open-ended '>= key' request; this is the only place where a WatchCreateRequest's RangeEnd is rewritten and then handed to the permission check, which is exactly the region the fix reorders.

fix_sites.entry_point: etcdserverpb.Watch/Watch bidirectional gRPC RPC, WatchCreateRequest (registered at server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/grpc.go:81)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The nearest sibling, the gRPC proxy's own watch permission check (server/proxy/grpcproxy/watch.go:213), lives in a separate binary/package and probes with a Range RPC instead of the auth store, so a solver can plausibly call it out of the advisory's scope; likewise an explicitly-present zero-length range_end is undocumented, which makes the Range route (server/etcdserver/v3_server.go:146) dismissible as an unsupported input shape.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A watch from a key by a user whose READ grant covers the open-ended range must keep working; mvcc distinguishes nil (single key, server/storage/mvcc/watcher_group.go:169) from []byte{} (>= key, :175), so the []byte{}/nil rewrite must remain in the handler for the watchStream.Watch call (server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/watch.go:339) after the permission check. Deleting the rewrite instead of moving it silently turns a legitimately authorized WithFromKey watch into a single-key watch.

O6_input_shapes: range_end absent (nil): exact-key watch, point-query authorization
range_end present with zero length ([]byte{}): must be treated as absent, i.e. point-query authorization
range_end any other non-empty value (WithPrefix / bounded range): interval-containment authorization

O7_producer.where: server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/watch.go:270-278 (recvLoop produces the nil/[]byte{} form consumed by watchStream.Watch at :339)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second watch front-end that normalizes cr.RangeEnd (for example turns the 0x00 open-ended sentinel into []byte{}, mirroring recvLoop) before issuing its permission-probe Range RPC at :252.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The proxy already re-implements watch authorization independently of v3rpc and already rewrites key/rangeEnd for the empty-key case at :214-219; a maintainer fixing the same class of bug here would naturally reuse the v3rpc normalization, and the check would then run on the translated value exactly as in the original bug.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A KV Range handler that normalizes RangeEnd with txn.mkGteRange (server/etcdserver/txn/delete.go:63-68) before EtcdServer.Range's auth check (server/etcdserver/v3_server.go:146).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RangeEnd sentinel translation already exists in two layers (server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/watch.go:275-278 and server/etcdserver/txn/delete.go:63-68), so a third normalization inside the KV handler is a plausible refactor that would reorder normalization ahead of authorization.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A cached or merged permission lookup that stores/keys permissions by an already-translated rangeEnd, so the point-vs-interval decision at :124 is made from the post-normalization value.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getMergedPerms already normalizes a grant's range_end at :43-51 and the comment block at :162-187 codifies the sentinel rules; caching on the translated representation is a natural optimization a maintainer could add there.

O9_family: authorization bypass / incorrect authorization (CWE-863): point-vs-interval misclassification in the RBAC range check

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change the classification in isRangeOpPermitted/checkKeyPoint (or delete the nil/[]byte{} rewrite outright) instead of reordering the handler, which either turns every exact-key read into an open-ended containment check or downgrades legitimate WithFromKey watches to single-key watches.

Whether an explicitly encoded zero-length range_end can reach a Go handler as a non-nil []byte{} depends on the protobuf runtime, which is not vendored in this tree. If it can, the Range/RangeStream/Txn range routes (server/etcdserver/v3_server.go:146,183; server/etcdserver/apply/auth.go:97,130,148) would check it as a point (server/auth/range_perm_cache.go:124) while mvcc executes it as open-ended (server/storage/mvcc/index.go:95-107), which is the same class of bug on a different sink; the documented wire sentinel '\0' (api/etcdserverpb/rpc.pb.go:2103-2108, api/etcdserverpb/rpc.proto:777-782) is checked correctly on those routes, so this is recorded as an adjacent observation, not as an O8 route
